transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-06-01
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Sam Lee (RiverMark Eng Mgr), Dana Ortiz (Platform), Michael Chen (SRE), Aisha Gomez (ML Eng)

Summary (auto): quick sync on latency tuning, TTFT, streaming, kernel tests, next steps captured

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call, hey Sam, Dana, Michael, Aisha?
[00:08] Sam: Hey Jordan, hi Priya, thanks. We should be good for 45.
[00:12] Priya: Great — I'll start with the perf numbers we ran overnight, then Jordan will run through roadmap items.
[00:18] Priya: So first off TTFT, we ran three variants: baseline (no streaming), streaming enabled, and streaming + fused attention kernel. For the baseline on our test workload (seq 256, batch 1) TTFT was sitting at about 170 to 210 ms, noisy depending on cold KV cache.
[00:33] Priya: With streaming enabled the apparent TTFT dropped to ~110-130ms because the pipeline starts sending tokens while decoding, so perceived latency improved. The fused attention kernel gave an additional ~10% TTFT improvement in median, down to ~100-120ms.
[00:48] Michael: Quick question — when you say fused attention, which kernel are we actually testing? The flash-attn variant or Redwood's fused kernel? We saw different results in our last run.
[00:56] Priya: Good call — this was Redwood fused (our custom fused attention path). We also tested flash-attn as a comparison and it was similar on H100 but slightly slower on A100 for these seq lengths. I'll put the matrix in the sheet.
[01:12] Dana: Is there any change in token quality when using fused or int8? We can't trade correctness for a small latency gain.
[01:18] Priya: For fused only (no quant) we didn't notice meaningful quality diffs. For int8 quantization we saw small regressions on some edge-case prompts — about a 1.5-2% failure rate on the eval set we ran. We're flagging those prompts.
[01:31] Aisha: Can you define failure rate — are these hallucinations or formatting issues?
[01:35] Priya: Mostly subtle formatting and occasionally missing tokens in enumerations, not gross hallucinations. We'll run the regen tests with a few seeds to confirm.
[01:42] Jordan: From a product perspective RiverMark's SLAs — Sam you mentioned a 120ms first-token goal for interactive flows?
[01:49] Sam: Yes, for the trader UI we want ~100-120ms TTFT ideally, 95th under 200. Background batch inference can be slower.
[01:58] Priya: Given those targets, streaming + fused is promising. But the caveat is backend warmup and KV cache. If the KV cache is cold the first request still pays a penalty around 250-400ms in our tests.
[02:12] Michael: How long does KV warm-up take on your Dedicated nodes? Because our traffic is spiky at market open and we may see many cold starts.
[02:19] Priya: Warm-up depends on sequence length and cache size. For seq 256 typical warm-up across a pool is ~15-45s for frequently hit prefixes. We have autoscale and pre-warm hooks we can discuss to mitigate opens.
[02:32] Jordan: Also worth noting you can pin a small warm pool for critical routes — that adds cost but keeps TTFT stable. We'll show cost delta.
[02:40] Sam: Cost is a factor. Send us the delta for Dedicated reserved vs Hosted for 2000 qps with these kernel settings.
[02:48] Priya: Will do. Next, sequence length tests: we ran seq 64/256/1024. At 1024 memory pressure caused more kernel switching and batch drops, which increased tail latency significantly. Best tradeoff seemed at 256 for your mixed workload.
[03:06] Aisha: For the longer sequences, did you try chunked streaming (prefix streaming) or sliding window?
[03:10] Priya: We did prefix streaming — it helps for perceived latency but increases downstream recombine complexity. We'll include an example trace.
[03:18] Jordan: I want to flag an imperfect transcription earlier — the internal artifact linked is the perf sheet: link shared in chat (we'll attach).
[03:25] Dana: On the kernel side, are we seeing GPU type differences? We tested H100 vs A100?
[03:29] Priya: Yes — H100 shines for larger seqs and fused kernels, A100 was fine at 256 but flash-attn had edge cases. We'll run a dedicated H100 vs A100 matrix.
[03:40] Michael: For our private deployment we may prefer H100 but procurement lead time is long — need to justify. If fused kernels on A100 give similar TTFT at 256 maybe we stick with A100s.
[03:51] Priya: Agree; we'll quantify perf per-dollar in the matrix.
[03:56] Sam: Any issues with SSO or audit logs when enabling debug traces? We need to ensure traces don't leak PII.
[04:03] Jordan: Good reminder — redaction can be enabled server side and our default traces are scrubbed; we'll provide the security docs for trace retention and KMS integration.
[04:12] Priya: Next I want to call out an anomaly at around 95th percentile for TTFT on one of the runs — looking at the logs it correlated with a GC spike on the host side and network retransmits. We'll capture both application and infra traces next run.
[04:26] Aisha: Can you capture the client timing as well? We want accurate client-perceived TTFT.
[04:30] Priya: Yes — Jordan will share instructions to attach client-side timestamps and we can merge with server traces.
[04:36] Jordan: Next steps — we'll do a kernel perf run across seq lengths 64/256/1024 on both A100 and H100; include fused, flash-attn, and baseline. Priya will own that.
[04:46] Sam: Also if fused + streaming gets us inside the 120ms median target and regressions are minimal, we'd like to schedule a pilot on Dedicated capacity for a week.
[04:56] Priya: Sounds good — we'll also include a quick cost estimate for a small warm pool vs auto-scaling only.
[05:02] Michael: For the int8 question, can you run a differential quality report on our core 50 prompts? We need to see exact diff examples.
[05:08] Priya: Yes Aisha will share the prompts and we'll run the int8 vs fp16 comparison; expect results in the kernel matrix doc.
[05:13] Jordan: Any blockers on your side?
[05:16] Sam: Procurement gating on Dedicated but decision will be data-driven. No blockers for tests.
[05:20] Dana: None. Just need timelines in writing.
[05:23] Jordan: We'll send updated timeline and spreadsheet by Thursday.
[05:26] Priya: Quick note — we saw slightly worse 95th tail at seq 1024 even with fused; the combination of kernel fallback and memory compaction causes jitter. Might need to tune batch size or eviction policy.
[05:39] Michael: Can you test smaller batches (batch 1-4) at 1024 and see tail effect?
[05:44] Priya: Yes will include.
[05:46] Sam: Ok let's recap concrete next steps.
[05:50] Jordan: Recap: Jordan to share perf sheet and trace upload instructions; Priya to run kernel comparison and int8 quality checks; Aisha to share 50 prompt templates; Michael to enable debug traces on next run. We'll aim to have initial matrix by 2027-06-07 and schedule deep dive the week of 2027-06-10 if results are promising.
[06:10] Aisha: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:13] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up in the thread with the docs and links.
[06:17] Sam: Thanks.

Note: timestamps above are approximate markers; full raw logs and perf sheets are in the shared drive link (see chat). Some transcription artifacts present: 'Redwood Dedicatedy' or 'flash attention' spelled inconsistently.
